chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibn Abi Nasr al-Baghdadi, from Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Muqri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il, from Abi Ishaq, from Shariḥ ibn Hanis, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) commanded us regarding the sacrificial animals (udhiyah) that we should inspect the eye and the ear, and He forbade us from the torn-eared, the split-horned, the one with a broken leg, and the one that is too weak to walk to the slaughter site.

key_terms.الْمُدَابَرَةِ: The one that is weak or too frail to walk to the place of slaughter
key_terms.الْمُقَابَلَةِ: The one with a broken leg (literally: facing/standing with difficulty)

ai.seo_question: What are the four specific defects that make a sacrificial animal invalid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the prophetic criteria for selecting sacrificial animals, emphasizing visual and auditory inspection to ensure quality while prohibiting specific defects like torn ears (*al-kharqa’*) and split horns (*al-sharqa’*). In Shia jurisprudence, these physical imperfections are critical for the validity of the *udhiyah*, reflecting the broader principle that offerings to God must be of the best and free from debilitating flaws.
